world.title: Mara Lin’s 2026 Work-and-Home Assistant World
world.premise: In 2026, Mara Lin is a mid-career operations program manager at Brightgrove Public Library Network (a regional nonprofit coordinating shared services for several local libraries). She relies on an assistant to juggle cross-team projects (vendor rollout, scheduling, internal comms), recurring meetings, and day-to-day logistics. At home, she shares a small rental townhouse with her partner and a dog, and the assistant helps coordinate chores, errands, meal planning, and family commitments. The same people and places recur across her work and personal life: colleagues in a few standing teams, a consistent set of neighborhood places, and stable tools used for planning, communication, and documentation. The benchmark world centers on ordinary, overlapping contexts—work projects with timelines and stakeholders, household routines, and practical preferences—without sensitive accounts or extraordinary events.

facts.statement: Mara Lin is an operations program manager on the Operations Programs Team at Brightgrove Public Library Network.
Nina Patel is Mara Lin’s manager at Brightgrove Public Library Network.
Owen Reed is the IT services lead at Brightgrove and is the main point of contact for systems rollouts and support workflows.
Sasha Kim is a communications specialist at Brightgrove and partners closely with Mara Lin in the Comms & Training Working Group.
Eli Mercado is a branch supervisor and a regular representative in the Branch Leads Council for frontline feedback.
Eli Mercado works at Riverbend Branch Library.
Devon Hart is Mara Lin’s partner in the Lin–Hart Household at Maple Street Townhouse.
Jordan Wu is Mara Lin’s neighbor and occasional running buddy, and is a go-to local contact for small favors like package pickup.
Mara Lin prefers Aurora Calendar to be treated as the source of truth for both work and personal scheduling.

Mara Lin prefers concise updates first (a short summary and next steps), with details available only if requested.
Mara Lin prefers to protect focus time in the mornings and schedule most meetings later in the day when possible.
When she needs a change of scene, Mara Lin prefers to do a work block at Hawthorn Coffee rather than at Brightgrove HQ.

facts.statement: For coordination with the IT Services Team, Mara Lin prefers to resolve issues asynchronously first and only schedule a live call with Owen Reed if it’s blocked.

During the Shift Coverage Pilot, Mara Lin runs a weekly check-in with the Branch Leads Council to gather feedback and confirm any process tweaks before they go network-wide.
The Knowledge Base Refresh is owned by the Operations Programs Team, with Mara Lin coordinating scope and milestones.

IT Services Team review is a required gate for any Knowledge Base Refresh changes that touch LanternDesk procedures, and Owen Reed is the approver for that review.

For Summer Reading Ops 2026, Sasha Kim partners with Mara Lin through the Comms & Training Working Group to prepare staff-facing updates and training announcements.
Mara Lin keeps quarterly project status check-ins for the Shift Coverage Pilot, Knowledge Base Refresh, and Summer Reading Ops 2026 scheduled as a recurring block in Aurora Calendar.

Nina Patel approved a documentation freeze for the Knowledge Base Refresh from 2026-04-20 through 2026-04-30 so the team could do a clean review pass and avoid midstream edits.
For Summer Reading Ops 2026, Mara Lin initially decided to run staff training as an in-person session at Brightgrove HQ to reduce confusion during rollout.

For Summer Reading Ops 2026, Mara Lin switched the training plan to a hybrid format: a shorter in-person session at Brightgrove HQ plus a recorded follow-up distributed by the Comms & Training Working Group.

To speed up final edits for the Knowledge Base Refresh, Mara Lin and Sasha Kim agreed to do a two-hour review working session at Hawthorn Coffee instead of trying to fit it into a packed HQ day.
Mara Lin decided that the official Shift Coverage Pilot request and approval templates would be maintained by the Operations Programs Team so updates stay centralized as the pilot evolves.

Mara Lin captures meeting notes in Pine Notes and ends each set of notes with a short action-items list labeled "Next steps".

Mara Lin routes operational or IT requests through LanternDesk rather than email, so they have an owner, status, and history.
For network-wide communications, Mara Lin gets Nina Patel’s sign-off before Sasha Kim sends anything out through the Comms & Training Working Group.
During the Shift Coverage Pilot, Mara Lin runs a weekly check-in with Owen Reed and Eli Mercado to review open issues and decide what needs escalation.
